description: Exploit the statistical regularity of real-world CSV files (where consecutive rows often have similar byte lengths) to speculatively predict the start offset of the next N rows, enabling prefetching and parallel parsing of predicted row boundaries. When prediction fails, fall back to exact scanning from the last confirmed boundary.
mathematical_formalization: Let L_i = byte length of row i. Predictor: L_hat_{i+1} = alpha * L_i + (1 - alpha) * L_bar. Predicted start of row i+k: S_hat_{i+k} = S_i + sum_{j=1}^{k} L_hat. Speedup: (1 - P_miss) * k * T_scalar / T_verify.
analogical_connections: CPU branch prediction: two-level adaptive predictor with global history
Video codec motion estimation: predicting offsets from neighboring data
Database cardinality estimation: histogram-based statistical models
implementation_hypothesis: Maintain rolling window of last 8 row lengths. Use EMA to predict next. Issue PREFETCHNTA for predicted row starts. Parse 8 predicted rows in parallel. Verify predictions by checking newline at predicted positions.
experiment_seed: Measure prediction accuracy on uniform-width, moderately-variable, and highly-variable CSV files. Compare EMA, median, and mode predictors.
